clue.text: Talk together about one tree

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the talking word goes round the numeral

parts.note: to confer is to talk things over together
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Two people chat about a single tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A pine or fir is a cone-bearing evergreen, a familiar kind of tree.

clue.text: Ape grabbing an awning

indicators.note: grabbing means holding, so the imitation word clutches the article inside it

parts.note: to ape someone is to copy them

explanation.surface: A monkey snatches hold of a shop awning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like the animal but works as the verb meaning to imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are an overhead covering of fabric giving shade or shelter.

clue.text: Extremely nervous about stake in French FC

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the edge letters go round the betting word
extremely asks for the extremes, the first and last letters, of the next word

parts.note: an ante is the stake put into the pot in poker

explanation.surface: Someone is very anxious about a bet on a French football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'nervous', but it takes that word's first and last letters, N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: FC Nantes is a professional football club from the city in western France.

clue.text: Fight corrupt sailor in Uruguayan port

parts.note: a fray is a fight or brawl
bent is slang for corrupt or dishonest
OS stands for ordinary seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A crooked seaman gets into a brawl in a South American harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: BENT is everyday British slang for crooked; Fray Bentos is also a well-known British brand of tinned pies, named after the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Fray Bentos is a town and river port on the Uruguay River in western Uruguay.

clue.text: About turn — swing back in the opposite direction

definitions.text: swing back in the opposite direction

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a turn is a performer's act on stage

explanation.surface: A soldier's about-turn swings round to face the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About turn' reads as a parade-ground command, but splits into 'About' (RE) and 'turn', a stage act.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond to a force by moving back against it is a reflex response.

clue.text: Flag-waver, quiet at unruly gathering

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly
a riot is a disorderly, violent crowd

explanation.surface: A nationalist keeps quiet at a violent demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who waves the national flag is a fervent lover of their country.

clue.text: Replica folded between two pages, held together by this?

indicators.note: between means the reworked letters sit inside the pair of page letters

parts.note: p is the standard abbreviation for page, taken twice

indicators.note: folded suggests the letters are bent into a new shape

explanation.surface: A copied document is folded and placed between two sheets fastened together.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a playful description of what keeps sheets fastened, rather than a dictionary synonym; 'folded' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bent wire loop is the everyday office tool that keeps sheets of paper clipped together.

clue.text: Look after a number, 500

parts.note: ten is a number
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Caring for a figure of five hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To care for or watch over someone or something.

clue.text: Great devotion to lady, I suspect, is apparent round start of romance

indicators.note: round means the reworked letters go around the single letter
suspect is used as an adjective meaning dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in this order
start of means take only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A man's intense devotion to a woman is plain once a romance begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' reworks TO LADY I into IDOLATY, which goes round R from 'romance'; 'is apparent' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship of idols, used loosely for excessive adoration or veneration of a person.

clue.text: Men, in principle, responsible for a block of flats

indicators.note: in means the men are placed inside the belief word

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief

explanation.surface: Men are, in principle, in charge of an apartment block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in principle' reads as a stock phrase, but 'in' is the container and 'principle' the TENET.
explanation.definitionFit: A large building divided into rented flats, especially an older crowded one in a city.

clue.text: Trained assassin from town in Japan

indicators.note: from means the answer is taken out of the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A trained killer comes from a Japanese town.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese mercenary agent trained in stealth and covert killing.

clue.text: Might this be blown till the cows come home?

definitions.text: Might this be blown till the cows come home?

parts.words: Might this be blown till the cows come home?
parts.note: till the cows come home normally means for ever, but here it is read literally: an instrument sounded in the Alps to call the herd back

explanation.surface: Something is played endlessly, until the cows return.
explanation.definitionFit: A long wooden horn used by Swiss herdsmen to call cattle down from mountain pastures.

clue.text: Try, by peers, errant body of church elders

indicators.note: errant means wandering astray, so the letters stray from their order

explanation.surface: A trial by one's peers goes wrong for a group of church elders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'errant' reworks the letters of TRY BY PEERS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Presbyterian churches the governing court of ministers and elders over a district.

clue.text: Friendly wife, member

parts.note: an arm is a member or limb of the body

explanation.surface: An affectionate wife joins as a member.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm greeting is a cordial, kindly one.

clue.text: Informed about holding search? One's doubtful

indicators.note: holding means the first pair of words wraps around the next pieces

parts.note: to be in on something is to be informed
on means about, as in a talk on a subject
a quest is a search
I is the Roman numeral for one; the apostrophe s is a link

explanation.surface: Someone who knows about the search admits to being unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's doubtful' looks like a single phrase, but 'One' gives I and only 'doubtful' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open to doubt is uncertain or under dispute.

clue.text: Eventually elected — article on drawn-out contest follows

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in
the is the definite article
long means drawn-out, lasting a great while
a run is a contest for office, as in a run for president

explanation.surface: A politician, at last elected after a long campaign, sees an article written about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'follows' just place the pieces after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Over a lengthy period, things finally turn out a certain way: ultimately.

clue.text: Rug is shock work of art

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it
a piece is a single artistic work

explanation.surface: A carpet is an alarming artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rug' looks like a floor covering, but it is slang for a wig; 'shock' looks like a fright but is a mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Rug is slang for a toupee or wig, worn to cover baldness.

clue.text: Surplus actors, gloomy

parts.note: over means left over or in excess
the cast is the company of actors in a play

explanation.surface: Too many actors make for a depressing production.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky covered with cloud is grey and dull.

clue.text: Written outline shows no care, is sloppy

indicators.note: sloppy means careless and messy, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A careless draft plot shows little effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloppy' reworks NO CARE IS; 'shows' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot summary or screenplay outline setting out a sequence of events.

clue.text: London station has choice fruit

parts.note: Victoria is a major railway terminus in London
a plum job is a choice, highly desirable one

explanation.surface: A London railway terminus offers top-quality fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: VICTORIA is one of London's main railway stations.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular English dessert variety of red-skinned stone fruit.

clue.text: Arrive at total

definitions.meaning: to reach a figure or decision
to add up to, as a bill does

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to reach a conclusion and to amount to a sum.

clue.text: Smear involving liberal leader during WWII

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the mark word wraps the single letter

parts.note: a stain is a smear or mark

explanation.surface: A smear campaign against a Liberal figure during the war.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin led the Soviet Union through the Second World War.

clue.text: Stinking row

definitions.meaning: a line or tier, as a taxi ... or a row of soldiers

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both foul-smelling and a line of people or things, as at a taxi stand.

clue.text: Baby's left a wet blanket

parts.note: read as baby is, meaning babies or pampers, which is spoils
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: An infant has abandoned a damp bedcover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby' is the verb to pamper; 'left' is the nautical left, PORT, not departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is someone who dampens others' fun, a killjoy.

clue.text: Bury's season with no games won

indicators.note: with no means the letter is removed from the season word

parts.note: winter is a season
W stands for won in sports results tables

explanation.surface: A Bury football team's season goes without a single win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the English football town, but it is the verb to entomb; W is 'won' in league tables.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a body is to place it in a grave.

clue.text: What king must do, reportedly, in check

indicators.note: reportedly means said out loud, so the spoken word is spelt differently

parts.note: a king must rule, that is reign

explanation.surface: A monarch's duty, as told, is to keep things under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' looks like chess, fitting 'king', but it means to restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to check or restrain, as with a horse's straps.

clue.text: Unison shown by soldiers during a salute

indicators.note: during means the soldiers come within the words for a salute

parts.note: to greet is to salute or hail
men is a common word for soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: Troops show perfect harmony as they give a salute.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in unison means being in accord, all of one mind.

clue.text: One Kent resort, perfect

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Deal is a seaside town in Kent

explanation.surface: A seaside town in Kent is described as flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is a seaside town in Kent, a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that matches a model of excellence is flawless.

clue.text: Thump counter, agitatedly

indicators.note: agitatedly means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone bangs a shop counter in agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat soundly or heavily defeat, as in a sporting thrashing.

clue.text: Find ladder below

parts.note: a ladder in tights or stockings is a run
down means below or beneath

explanation.surface: Locate the stepladder underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'ladder' in British English is a run in tights, not the climbing kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To track down something after a search is to locate it.
